query: What visit-note signals suggest a longer visit?

per_column.name: procedural_intervention_present
per_column.rationale: Interventions performed plausibly drive visit length, a strong analytical axis. But values overreach: the annual-physical row (labs only, no med change) and the MI follow-up ('continue current regimen') are both tagged 'medication_change' though no change occurred; the knee-injury row is tagged 'procedure_performed' when only an MRI was ordered. Frequent invented interventions weaken grounding.

per_column.name: diagnostic_workup_scope
per_column.rationale: Labs/imaging ordered is a clean, useful predictor of visit workup effort. Sample values track the text well: 'both_ordered' for physical with labs (note says only labs though—slight overreach), 'labs_ordered' for repeat lipid panel, 'imaging_ordered' for MRI, 'not_present' for viral URI. Largely sound.

per_column.name: clinical_severity_level
per_column.rationale: Severity is a reasonable driver of visit duration and gives a gradable axis. Sampled values are well-warranted: mild for stable follow-ups, moderate for acne/knee injury. Grounded readings of the notes.

per_column.name: emergency_critical_status
per_column.rationale: Emergency escalation would strongly affect duration, but in this outpatient-skewed sample it is 'not_present' for 189 rows, making it near-constant and thus offering limited grouping leverage here. Values shown are correctly 'not_present'; well grounded.

per_column.name: specialist_consultation_or_referral
per_column.rationale: Referrals/consults plausibly add visit time and give a useful categorical axis. Mostly grounded; the knee row is labeled 'referral_arranged' though the note only mentions ordering an MRI, not an explicit referral—mild overreach but defensible for orthopedic workup.

per_column.name: counseling_education_complexity
per_column.rationale: Counseling/education time is a genuine driver of longer visits. Some values are inferred beyond the text: the physical exam row is tagged 'lifestyle_behavior_change' though the note only records fatigue and labs with no documented counseling; MI follow-up 'medication_education' is plausible but not explicit. Mixed grounding.

per_column.name: comorbidity_or_multisystem_scope
per_column.rationale: Multisystem burden is a reasonable duration predictor. But the annual-physical row is labeled 'multiple_active_comorbidities' when the note describes a largely well patient (mild fatigue, single labs)—an unsupported assertion. Other samples (single_system, end_organ for post-MI) are sound. Notable overreach.

judge.rationale: The added columns collectively give strong, genuinely useful axes (interventions, workup scope, severity, referrals, counseling, comorbidity burden) directly relevant to predicting visit duration, well beyond generic length/sentiment flags. emergency_critical_status is near-constant in this sample and offers weaker leverage. Groundedness is generally good—silent rows correctly get 'not_present'—but several columns over-assert: 'medication_change' where regimens are continued, 'procedure_performed' for an ordered MRI, and 'multiple_active_comorbidities' for an essentially well patient. These recurring confident-specific inferences pull groundedness down modestly, though most values remain sound readings of the notes.
